prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop landing-page composition comp
Primary request: Render the Vista landing page edge to edge at a 16:10 desktop viewport, no browser chrome and no room around it. Vista is a native virtual-machine app for Apple silicon. Make the page itself a Commodore 128-era graphical operating system: a cobalt desktop in a warm molded-plastic frame, with one oversized working “VISTA 128” terminal window as the dominant move rather than a modern hero.
Content: a narrow menu bar has “VISTA  FILE  MACHINE  WINDOW  HELP” and right-aligned “0.1.0”. The main terminal window prints “NATIVE VIRTUAL MACHINES FOR APPLE SILICON”, “READY.”, the install command “brew install --cask wess/packages/vista”, and a prompt where visitors can type CATALOG, INSTALL, DOCS, SECURITY, or CLEAR. A smaller catalog window lists macOS, Ubuntu, Fedora, Debian, BSD, and experimental Windows 11 Arm with honest status markers. A compact system monitor shows “0 TELEMETRY / 1 PROCESS PER GUEST / APFS SNAPSHOTS”. The primary action is an obvious physical-style “DOWNLOAD 0.1.0” control in the terminal window.
Composition: overlapping but readable OS windows create depth; the terminal owns most of the viewport, catalog and monitor tuck behind it, and a documentation/manual band begins below.
Visual law: cobalt and periwinkle screen fields, warm putty plastic, dark brown legends, orange selected controls and one green ready light. Pixel bitmap type for screen content; compact industrial grotesk for case labels. Crisp and functional, no neon green, no glossy 3D, no gradients, no SaaS cards, no split hero, no floating badges.
